items.title: The eta invariant is multiplicative in the nonzerodivisor: eta_f eta_g equals eta_fg
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, nonzerodivisors f and g in A, and a complex M^bullet of A-modules such that fg is a nonzerodivisor on every M^i, and asserts the identity eta_f eta_g M^bullet = eta_fg M^bullet (source lines 27839-27844). The second application of eta is to the already-transformed complex, so the two sides live in different localizations, and the proof must say in what sense the identity is meant: objectwise, the statement is that in each degree i the two constructions yield the same submodule of M^i_{fg} = (M^i_g)_f (proof lines 27846-27848). That comparison of submodules under the identification of the two-fold localization is the content of the lemma, and the author leaves the details to the reader.
